text: The 2022 loss in native forest on this rural property (17.6 ha) involved approximately 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss, which was corroborated by multiple Earth-observation datasets. The event occurred within a mapped native forest area (0.5 ha), with no indication of planted forest involvement. However, the evidence does not specify the cause of the loss—it could have been due to harvesting, fire, storms, or other disturbances. The data also does not establish whether the loss was legal, authorized, or illegal, nor does it identify the responsible actor. The observation was confirmed by cross-referencing Hansen Global Forest Change data with the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 reference map, ensuring reliability.
